response.query: Provide studies relevant to: Reassessing the Evidence for the Composite Bow in Ancient Eurasia, topics discussed:
response.answer: Recent studies reassess evidence for the composite bow in ancient Eurasia, focusing on its construction, effectiveness, and spread across cultures. Key findings highlight its superior range and power compared to simple bows. Research emphasizes archaeological and historical data to support these conclusions.

results.content: med’uolda ‘having been born’ me qadaa ~ maqadaa ‘somewhere’ e ~ o jolle ~ jollo ‘moss’ möŋer ~ moŋor ‘noise’ i ~ a waγine ~ waγane ~ ‘personal’ saabind’e ~ saaband’e ‘fishing net’ jalmisče ~ jalmasče ‘third’ arinn’e- ~ arann’e- ‘to be deft’ i ~ e n’iŋil’ite- ~ n’iŋil’ete- ‘to abuse each other’ paad’iduo ~ paad’eduo ‘daughter’ čiribe ~ čirebe ‘plummet’ maranmi ~ maranme ‘simply’ jeleklisče ~ jeleklesče ‘forth’ u ~ e surun’e- ~ suren’e- ‘to be fat’ jeruguu ~ jereguu ‘plain’ n’angumu ~ n’angemu ‘purposely’ unmun ~ enmun ‘every’ -pul ~ -pel ‘PL’ u ~ i saburqa ~ sabirqa ‘plane’ - consonants: d ~ r čuŋde ~ čuŋre ‘mind, thought’ jaŋde ~ jaŋre ‘goose’ 6 r ~ s ugurče ~ ugusče ‘foot, leg’ n’ ~ m n’id’erpe- ~ mid’erpe- ‘to be new’ n’ ~ n ten’i ~ teni ‘here’ ŋ ~ n suŋdii- ~ sundii- ‘to throw around’ tiŋŋii ~ tiŋnii- ‘to grudge’ j ~ l’ juku ~ l’uku ‘small’ - variation at morpheme boundaries: - adverb formation: maaruojneŋ ~ maaruolneŋ ‘happily’ (-neŋ ‘ADV’) - nominalized participles: solγid’e ‘gathering’ ~ solγind’eγa ‘at a gathering’ (-d’e ~ -nd’e ‘PTCP’) - variation at word boundaries: wadun aruu ~ wadud aruu ‘the Yukaghir language’ tude gedeγane ~ tude kedelγane ‘himself’ el taat pan ~ el taat ban ‘[it] is not like that’ taat kurčiinuni ~ taat gurčiinuni ‘[it] used to happen so’ It is hard to say whether these alternations are influenced by dialectal differences.
